justification: Contributes a selective policy for what context persists across sessions; evidence is a lab comparison of selective vs no-memory vs full-history conditions, not a field study of use.

Contribution is a taxonomy and information-theoretic framing of context accumulation failure (an audit of one named mechanism); evidence is calibrated simulation comparing MCP vs Skills, not a real deployment.
Contributes an architectural taxonomy plus measurement of 22 frameworks, i.e. an instrument for measuring loop behaviour; evidence is lab runs on BBH, GSM8K and ARC.
Headline artefact is the XEPV trace-encoding and n-gram/Markov diagnostic framework over execution traces; studied on a production ReAct system with a natural before/after deployment.
AnalysisBench is the instrument, 35 tool-project pairs for measuring agent behaviour; the agents are run in the lab on that benchmark, not in production.
SWIFT's contribution is synthesising the workflow topology itself (structural priors transferring topology across tasks); evidence is lab results on five plus four benchmarks.
Novelty is executability as the judgement signal, execution-aware planning and execution-result verification; validated in the lab on WebQSP and CWQ.
Contribution is anchoring plan construction in a deterministic FSM that fixes the Design-Verify-Rectify step order (gating is the runner-up); evaluated on the extended BioProBench benchmark.
PHMForge is an evaluation environment with 99 scenarios and 39 MCP tools, an instrument rather than a loop mechanism; agents are scored in that lab harness.

Contribution is removing the fixed turn-to-turn orchestration policy so the completion itself determines the next step, formalised as agentic machines; support is demonstration runs, no measured benchmark.
ScrambleToolBench is the artefact, an interactive benchmark isolating behavioural discovery; SOTA models are measured on it in the lab.
Argues for a System-2 coordination layer and proposes the MACI stack (debate, filtering, persistence) as a new framing of the field; empirical part contrasts static prompting with adaptive control.
SaaSBench is the instrument, 30 long-horizon tasks with 5370 validation nodes; agents are measured on it in the lab.
Contribution is branching over notebook-cell nodes with entropy-based information-gain path selection (POMDP over a dynamic tree); validated on InfiAgent-DABench and DS-Bench.
Contributes five agentic maturity metrics (DC, TSR, ARC, HIC, TCT) for measuring workflow behaviour; applied descriptively to four IDE agents on one constructed development task.
The claim is the closed-loop correction of erroneous guesses from MLFF relaxation feedback (the checker is off-the-shelf physics); validated on AA20 and OCD-GMAE62 with DFT checks.
AssetOpsBench is a benchmarking framework with 140+ queries and a simulated IoT environment; agents are evaluated inside that simulation, not in live operations.
Contributes a defect ontology and control-preservation scoring for measuring execution processes; instantiated on 200 cases drawn from AndroidBench, TerminalBench and SWE-bench-Verified.
Retrieved State-Goal-Action atoms are re-grounded to determine the next action, so the stored state drives step selection rather than window fitting; validated on complex planning benchmarks.

Contribution is explicit control-flow machinery, a rooted capability tree with a LIFO stack execution loop and lazy discovery; evidence is controlled benchmarks varying catalog size and workflow depth.
Contribution is the nested layered stewardship topology arranging legacy applications as agents under a central orchestrator; proposed and argued only, with no evaluation reported.

Contribution is per-peer credibility and peer-relationship evidence used for routing and reliability-weighted voting among agents; tested by inducing counterfactual reliability shifts across five models.

Contribution is an inter-agent artifact synchronisation protocol (MESI invalidation, formal mapping and theorem); evidence is TLA+ verification plus simulation over four varied workload configurations.
AgentGit contributes state commit, revert and branching machinery that lets the loop return to an earlier step; evidence is a multi-step A/B test against LangGraph, AutoGen and Agno.
The mechanism is a calibrated abstention check deciding whether a sub-agent may answer or must escalate; studied in a live large-scale production e-commerce assistant.
